findings.body: The sender allowlist is enforced only when this turn-start call runs. When a turn is already active, live-execution.ts:263–271 routes directly through live-recovery-coordinator.ts:447–461, bypassing decideBatch. live-turn-routing.ts:48–55 checks only requiredContinuationUserId, not the configured sender allowlist. Consequently, a disallowed sender's mid-turn request is forwarded to the agent despite the promised continuation gate. Apply the policy before forwarding active-turn input, keeping refused messages as history.
findings.title: Not done: Mention-required groups follow the conversation

findings.body: This timestamp interval also matches turns that never ran an agent. live-execution.ts:281–287 claims a live turn before invoking the processor at line 317; an unmentioned batch returns successfully without running the agent, and the wrapper finalizes that claim as completed at lines 339–357. An unrelated message saved after that batch was taken but before its claim ends is therefore marked receivedDuringTurn and starts an agent turn later. Record whether the agent actually ran rather than treating every claimed interval as agent activity.
findings.title: Distinguish an actual running turn from a rejected admission

findings.body: The new end-to-end scenario exercises a Slack thread follow-up and unrelated history, but not a split mention batch, a direct reply to the bot, or mid-turn allowlist enforcement. Its helper invokes processGroupMessages directly, bypassing the active-turn admission path. The new mid-turn integration case merely claims a row and transitions it from claimed to completed (live-admission-work-items.postgres.integration.test.ts:243–255); it never runs an agent. Extend the existing owner scenario through live admission with a held runner and an actual sender policy so these promised behaviours and routing defects are observable.
findings.title: Not done: mention-required conversation end-to-end coverage

findings.body: The Functional check paragraphs exercise Slack thread continuation, unrelated history, and a repository-seeded claimed interval. They omit split-message continuation, a direct reply to the bot, and sender allowlist enforcement. The claimed-to-completed fixture here also never starts a runner, so it cannot substantiate the claimed check of a message arriving while the agent was working. Exercise the remaining covered paths through the runtime and update the Functional check with their observed outcomes.
findings.title: Not done: functional check

findings.body: The thread lookup reads only pageSize rows from the beginning. canonical-message-repository.postgres.ts:626–631 orders these rows ascending and applies the limit. If a Telegram topic or another thread has 200 human messages before the bot first replies, subsequent unmentioned follow-ups are refused forever because that bot reply never enters the inspected page. Use a scoped outbound existence query or continue paging until a bot reply is found.
findings.title: Find bot replies beyond the first history page

findings.body: Matching any route's textual trigger sets a shared mentionsBot flag. channel-persistence-handlers.ts:223–233 persists that same message for every matching route, and decideBatch accepts the flag without checking the current route's trigger. With @Helper and @Planner routes in one Telegram group, '@Helper do this' therefore starts both agents; previously each processor checked its own trigger. Reserve the shared flag for native bot mentions, or preserve route-specific trigger attribution through fan-out, including captions.
findings.title: Keep textual route triggers specific to their agent
